newsitem.title: SPAIN: Mexico must grow 6 pct/yr to create jobs -- Ortiz.
newsitem.headline: Mexico must grow 6 pct/yr to create jobs -- Ortiz.

text.p: The Mexican economy needs to grow by at least six percent a year to make a dent in unemployment and poverty, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said on Monday.

"My country needs to reach a rhythm of growth of no less than six percent a year so that Spain can create the number of jobs the population demands and to effectively fight poverty," he told the annnual general meeting of the Inter-American Development Bank in Barcelona.
In 1996, the Mexican economy grew just 5.1 percent, surpassing expectations with a swift rebound from the economic crisis triggered by a shock peso devaluation in December 1994.
Future growth must be secured with public and private investment, Ortiz told the annual general meeting of the Inter-American Development Bank in Barcelona.
Ortiz said that in 1997 exports were expected to reach a record of $110 billion, representing 40 percent of the total exports expected in Latin American.

"In an environment of greater certainty and stability, we will be able to consolidate sustainable growth that is being extended to all productive sectors and is generating higher living standards for all," Ortiz said.
